shorts.title: Cruz: "I think it was a mistake." Trump's Putin gift #Shorts
shorts.hook: Even Ted Cruz says Trump blew it
shorts.narration: [sarcastic] Friends, Ted Cruz just said something true on Fox News. Quote: "I wish the president hadn't done it. I think it was a mistake." The it? President Trump waiving key Russia sanctions and tariffs. [beat] Nikki Haley called it, quote, "a terrible misjudgment of Putin." Senator Thom Tillis, a Republican, said "beyond irresponsible." [deadpan] When Cruz and Tillis agree on something, check the sky for flying pigs. Then Trump said, quote, "A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet." [beat] Sir, you signed the order. [serious] George Washington warned about, quote, "the insidious wiles of foreign influence." He did not add a footnote that said, unless diesel is pricey. [beat] The waiver follows rising fuel prices, per reports. So is Putin the energy secretary now? [mischievously] Subscribe. Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Trump: "We didn't like what we were reading" — Guilfoyle out #Shorts
shorts.hook: "We didn't like what we were reading"
shorts.narration: [incredulous] Friends, the ambassador to Greece is out. Kimberly Guilfoyle. The White House press secretary said, quote, "We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign." [beat] Trump put it this way: "We didn't like what we were reading." [deadpan] Fair. Reading is hard. What was he reading? The Wall Street Journal reported she allegedly asked a Trump donor to pay about a hundred thousand dollars on her American Express card, shortly before her Senate confirmation hearing. She calls the allegations false, and her lawyer says the messages aren't authentic. [beat] The donor reportedly said no, because it would cost him his marriage. [sarcastic] Even the donor had a better ethics office than the administration. The Constitution says the President shall appoint ambassadors with the Senate's advice and consent. [beat] Not with the donor's credit-card limit. Subscribe. Dylan Avanti, every day, from the Left Coast.

Guilfoyle called the allegations false; her attorney Jesse Binnall said the messages attributed to her were not authentic.
Deters allegedly declined, telling her it would cost him his marriage, per messages shared with the Journal.

shorts.title: Vance: "D.C. is a corrupt town." Then he said this about Trump #Shorts
shorts.hook: Vance: "Yes, D.C. is a corrupt town"
shorts.narration: [amused] Friends, Vice President JD Vance sat down with CBS in Michigan and admitted something. Quote: "Yes, D.C. is a corrupt town." [beat] Who runs D.C. right now? Asked about Trump, he said, quote, "I have not seen a single shred of evidence that he participates or sanctions in that corruption." [deadpan] Not a shred. He's looking very hard in the other direction. He also said, quote, "If somebody's selling access to the White House, that's disgusting and despicable." [beat] Agreed! The anchor had just raised reports about Trump's crypto earnings and a fired ambassador. [sarcastic] Vance would follow the law on subpoenas if Democrats win. Quote: "Of course I will." We'll hold him to it. James Madison wrote, quote, "If men were angels, no government would be necessary." [beat] Nobody told the White House gift shop. Subscribe. Dylan Avanti roasts the news from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Ilhan Omar's home searched weeks before the midterms #Shorts
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, federal agents searched Representative Ilhan Omar's Washington home this month. The Justice Department says it was a judicially authorized warrant in an ongoing criminal investigation, and it hasn't said what the probe is about. [beat] Omar says, quote, "this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement." She also said, "I will not be silenced." A former official told NPR it concerns immigration fraud allegations, and Vice President Vance has alleged immigration fraud before, which she denies. [deadpan] Now, there's a Justice Department guideline against publicly probing candidates within sixty days of an election. [beat] It's not binding, and NPR notes the department hasn't always followed it. The Fourth Amendment protects, quote, "the right of the people to be secure in their persons, houses, papers, and effects." [serious] Fair process matters, whoever the target is. Subscribe for the daily news.

shorts.title: Trump's $5,000 "dividend" — no plan, no price tag, no Congress #Shorts
shorts.narration: [amused] Friends, at the Republican convention in Dallas, President Trump promised every American adult a five-thousand-dollar "Trump Dividend" if Republicans keep Congress. [beat] He urged voters to, quote, "pretend he's on the ballot." [deadpan] Sir, you are not on the ballot. Details on funding? None. Implementation? The White House didn't respond to questions. Fox 10 reports the cost would likely top a trillion dollars. [sarcastic] Vance then suggested it might skip the wealthy and be paid for by tariffs. So, a dividend, but only if you win, and only if someone else pays. [beat] That's not a dividend, that's a raffle with a cabinet. The Constitution says, quote, "No Money shall be drawn from the Treasury, but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law." Budget experts say he'd need Congress. [beat] So, Republicans: do you vote for the check, or for the lecture on the deficit? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti, from the Left Coast.

claims.text: At the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Trump pledged a $5,000 'Trump Dividend' to every American adult if Republicans keep control of Congress.
The article reports Trump urged voters to 'pretend he's on the ballot.'
He gave no details on funding or implementation; the White House did not respond to questions seeking clarification.
The payments would likely cost more than $1 trillion.
Vance appeared to temper the pledge, suggesting payments might exclude wealthy Americans and could be funded through tariff revenues.
Marc Goldwein of the Committee for Responsible Federal Budget said Trump would need congressional approval.
Article I, Section 9: 'No Money shall be drawn from the Treasury, but in Consequence of Appropriations made by Law.'
